docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Frequenz gRPC API to retrieve data from regulated market metering points.

docs.title: Supported Platforms
docs.text:
The following platforms are officially supported (tested):

  • Python: 3.11
  • Operating System: Ubuntu Linux 20.04
  • Architectures: amd64, arm64

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: If you want to know how to build this project and contribute to it, please check out the Contributing Guide.

docs.title: Contributing to Frequenz Market Metering API
Build
docs.text:
You can use build to simply build the source and binary distribution:

python -m pip install build
python -m build

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
You need to make sure you have the git submodules updated:

git submodule update --init

docs.title: Running protolint
docs.text:
To make sure some common mistakes are avoided and to ensure a consistent style it is recommended to run protolint. After you installed protolint, just run:

protolint lint proto

docs.title: Python setup
docs.text:
You can use editable installs to develop the project locally (it will install all the dependencies too):

python -m pip install -e .

This will also generate the Python files from the proto/ files and leave them in py/, so you can inspect them.

Or you can install all development dependencies (mypy, pylint, pytest, etc.) in one go too: 

python -m pip install -e .[dev]

If you don't want to install all the dependencies, you can also use nox to run the tests and other checks creating its own virtual environments:

python -m pip install .[dev-noxfile]
nox

You can also use nox -R to reuse the current testing environment to speed up test at the expense of a higher chance to end up with a dirty test environment.

docs.title: Upgrading dependencies
docs.text:
If you want to update the dependency frequenz-api-common, then you need to:

  1. Update the submodule frequenz-api-common
  2. Update the version of the frequenz-api-common package in pyproject.toml

The version of frequenz-api-common used in both places mentioned above should be the same.

Here is an example of upgrading the frequenz-api-common dependency to version v0.2.0: 

ver="0.2.0"
ver_minor=$(echo $ver | cut -d. -f1,2)

cd submodules/frequenz-api-common
git remote update
git checkout v${ver}
cd -

sed 's/frequenz-api-common == [0-9]\.[0-9]\.[0-9]/frequenz-api-common == '"${ver}/" -i pyproject.toml
sed 's|https://frequenz-floss.github.io/frequenz-api-common/v[0-9]\.[0-9]/objects.inv|https://frequenz-floss.github.io/frequenz-api-common/v'${ver_minor}'/objects.inv|' -i mkdocs.yml

docs.title: Running tests / checks individually
docs.text:
For a better development test cycle you can install the runtime and test dependencies and run pytest manually.

python -m pip install .[dev-pytest]  # included in .[dev] too

# And for example
pytest tests/test_*.py

Or you can use nox:

nox -R -s pytest -- test/test_*.py

The same appliest to pylint or mypy for example:

nox -R -s pylint -- test/test_*.py
nox -R -s mypy -- test/test_*.py

docs.title: Building the documentation
docs.text:
To build the documentation, first install the dependencies (if you didn't install all dev dependencies):

python -m pip install -e .[dev-mkdocs]

Then you can build the documentation (it will be written in the site/ directory):

mkdocs build

Or you can just serve the documentation without building it using:

mkdocs serve

Your site will be updated live when you change your files (provided that you used pip install -e ., beware of a common pitfall of using pip install without -e, in that case the API reference won't change unless you do a new pip install).

To build multi-version documentation, we use mike. If you want to see how the multi-version sites looks like locally, you can use:

mike deploy my-version
mike set-default my-version
mike serve

mike works in mysterious ways. Some basic information:

  • mike deploy will do a mike build and write the results to your local gh-pages branch. my-version is an arbitrary name for the local version you want to preview.
  • mike set-default is needed so when you serve the documentation, it goes to your newly produced documentation by default.
  • mike serve will serve the contents of your local gh-pages branch. Be aware that, unlike mkdocs serve, changes to the sources won't be shown live, as the mike deploy step is needed to refresh them.

Be careful not to use --push with mike deploy, otherwise it will push your local gh-pages branch to the origin remote.

That said, if you want to test the actual website in your fork, you can always use mike deploy --push --remote your-fork-remote, and then access the GitHub pages produced for your fork.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
These are the steps to create a new release:

  1. Get the latest head you want to create a release from.

  2. Update the RELEASE_NOTES.md file if it is not complete, up to date, and remove template comments (<!-- ... ->) and empty sections. Submit a pull request if an update is needed, wait until it is merged, and update the latest head you want to create a release from to get the new merged pull request.

  3. Create a new signed tag using the release notes and a semver compatible version number with a v prefix, for example:

git tag -s --cleanup=whitespace -F RELEASE_NOTES.md v0.0.1

  1. Push the new tag.

  2. A GitHub action will test the tag and if all goes well it will create a GitHub Release, and upload a new package to PyPI automatically.

  3. Once this is done, reset the RELEASE_NOTES.md with the template:

cp .github/RELEASE_NOTES.template.md RELEASE_NOTES.md

Commit the new release notes and create a PR (this step should be automated eventually too).

  1. Celebrate!

docs.title: Cross-Arch Testing
docs.text:
This project has built-in support for testing across multiple architectures. Currently, our CI conducts tests on arm64 machines using QEMU emulation. We also have the flexibility to expand this support to include additional architectures in the future.

This project contains Dockerfiles that can be used in the CI to test the python package in non-native machine architectures, e.g., arm64. The Dockerfiles exist in the directory .github/containers/nox-cross-arch, and follow a naming scheme so that they can be easily used in build matrices in the CI, in nox-cross-arch job. The naming scheme is:

<arch>-<os>-python-<python-version>.Dockerfile

E.g.,

arm64-ubuntu-20.04-python-3.11.Dockerfile

If a Dockerfile for your desired target architecture, OS, and python version does not exist here, please add one before proceeding to add your options to the test matrix.

docs.title: ActivateMarketLocationRequest
docs.text:
Request to activate one or more Market Locations.

Activation marks the Market Location as active again for normal operations, allowing new sample ingestion and inclusion in default listings. Historical samples, revisions, and metadata remain unchanged.

Field Type Label Description market_locations MarketLocationSelector repeated List of Market Locations to activate.

docs.title: ActivateMarketLocationResponse
docs.text:
Response for batch activation of Market Locations.

A Result entry is returned per MarketLocationRef, regardless of whether the operation succeeded or failed. Structured error codes allow clients to implement automated handling and retries.

Field Type Label Description results MarketLocationOperationResult repeated Activation results, one per market location from the request.

docs.title: CreateMarketLocationRequest
docs.text:
Creates a new Market Location within the clients authorized enterprise scope.

A Market Location represents a contract-level metering point identifier used in regulated electricity markets (e.g., MaLo in Germany, MPAN in the UK, ESI-ID in the US, or NMI in Australia). This RPC registers such a Market Location with the platform.

!!! example "Example Request" 

{
  "market_location_selector": {
    "market_area": "MARKET_AREA_EU_DE",
    "market_location_id": {
      "id": {
        "value": "DE01234567890"
      },
      "type": "MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_MALO_ID"
    }
  },
  "market_location": {
    "display_name": "Main Office – Consumption",
    "supported_directions": [
      "ENERGY_FLOW_DIRECTION_IMPORT"
    ],
    "time_resolution": "TIME_RESOLUTION_15_MIN",
    "payload": {
      "siteCode": "HQ-North",
      "comment": "Primary billing meter"
    }
  }
}

Field Type Label Description market_location_selector MarketLocationSelector Identifies the Market Location within the client's authorized enterprise scope.

!!! important The combination of market_area and market_location_id must be unique within the authorized enterprise scope. | | market_location | MarketLocation | | Metadata describing the Market Location.

All fields except payload must be populated. The service validates the provided configuration and assigns lifecycle metadata such as revisions and timestamps during creation. |

docs.title: DeactivateMarketLocationRequest
docs.text:
Request to deactivate one or more Market Locations.

Deactivation marks each Market Location as inactive for future operations, without deleting historical metadata or time-series samples. This aligns with regulatory expectations: Market Locations must remain auditable even when they are no longer active.

A deactivated Market Location: • cannot receive new samples, • is omitted from default listing operations (unless explicitly requested), • retains all historical revisions for audit, reporting, and compliance.

Field Type Label Description market_locations MarketLocationSelector repeated List of Market Locations to deactivate.

docs.title: DeactivateMarketLocationResponse
docs.text:
Response for batch deactivation of Market Locations.

Each entry in results corresponds to a market location from the request and reports whether the operation succeeded, failed, or was skipped (e.g., already inactive).

The RPC never deletes historical data; it only changes activation state.

Field Type Label Description results MarketLocationOperationResult repeated Deactivation results, one per market location from the request.

docs.title: ListMarketLocationsRequest
docs.text:
Lists Market Locations with optional filters and revision-selection controls.

!!! note "Pagination" Pagination is supported via pagination_params. The server may return fewer results than requested. Use the returned pagination_info to continue paging, or stop when next_page_token is empty.

!!! example "Example Request: Filter by two Market Location IDs" 

{
  "filter": {
    "market_location_id_filters": [
      {
        "value": "DE01234567890",
        "type": "MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_MALO_ID"
      },
      {
        "value": "DE09876543210",
        "type": "MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_MALO_ID"
      }
    ],
    "activation_filter": "ACTIVATION_FILTER_ONLY_ACTIVE"
  },
  "revision_selection": {
    "revision_strategy": "REVISION_STRATEGY_ALL",
    "changed_fields": [
      "MARKET_LOCATION_CHANGED_FIELD_SUPPORTED_DIRECTIONS",
      "MARKET_LOCATION_CHANGED_FIELD_TIME_RESOLUTION"
    ]
  },
  "pagination_params": {
    "page_size": 100
  }
}

Field Type Label Description filter MarketLocationsFilter Optional filtering criteria for narrowing the result set. revision_selection MarketLocationRevisionSelection Optional revision-selection filter controlling if latest, all or selected revisions are returned.

Additionally historical revisions can be filtered by changed fields. If omitted the service only returns the latest revision. | | pagination_params | frequenz.api.common.v1alpha8.pagination.PaginationParams | | Pagination parameters. |

docs.title: MarketLocation
docs.text:
Represents a logical Market Location used in regulated electricity markets.

A Market Location is a contract-level metering point identifier defined by the local jurisdiction (e.g., MaLo in Germany, MPAN in the UK, ESI-ID in the US, NMI in Australia). It abstracts from physical meters or channels and is the anchor for billing, settlement, reconciliation, forecasting, and portfolio aggregation.

!!! example "Example Market Location Object" 

{
  "display_name": "Main Office – Consumption",
  "supported_directions": ["ENERGY_FLOW_DIRECTION_IMPORT"],
  "time_resolution": "TIME_RESOLUTION_15_MIN",
  "payload": {
    "cost_center": "CC-1103",
    "site_group": "HQ-North",
    "notes": "Primary billing meter"
  }
}

Field Type Label Description display_name string Optional human-readable name for organizational use. supported_directions EnergyFlowDirection repeated Supported energy-flow directions for this Market Location.

Indicates which energy-flow directions this Market Location is permitted to represent according to regulatory or contractual rules.

!!! note "What supported_directions means" This field reflects the contractual capability of the Market Location to represent import (consumption), export (generation), or both. It does not describe physical wiring or real-time flow, but the officially registered role in the market.

!!! examples "Market Location Examples" • Germany (DE) - Consumption MaLo → [IMPORT] - Feed-in MaLo → [EXPORT]

• UK (MPAN) - A single MPAN may support both directions → [IMPORT, EXPORT] | | time_resolution | TimeResolution | | Primary contractual time resolution for this Market Location.

This describes the default metering interval (e.g., PT15M, PT30M, PT5M). It reflects the settlement granularity expected by the jurisdiction.

!!! note Some markets provide multiple resolutions. This is metadata describing the primary resolution (e.g., PT15M). | | payload | google.protobuf.Struct | | Optional user-defined metadata.

Clients may store arbitrary structured data (e.g., cost centers, internal references, grouping labels, billing metadata). |

docs.title: MarketLocationDetail
docs.text:
Detailed representation of a Market Location, including metadata necessary for revision management, activation state, and lifecycle tracking.

MarketLocationDetail wraps the immutable identity fields and semantic attributes contained in MarketLocation with operational metadata.

!!! example "Example MarketLocationDetail Object" 

{
  "market_location_ref": {
    "enterprise_id": 42,
    "market_area": "MARKET_AREA_EU_DE",
    "market_location_id": {
      "value": "DE01234567890",
      "type": "MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_MALO_ID"
    }
  },
  "market_location": {
    "display_name": "Main Office – Consumption",
    "supported_directions": ["ENERGY_FLOW_DIRECTION_IMPORT"],
    "time_resolution": "TIME_RESOLUTION_15_MIN"
  },
  "revision": 3,
  "is_active": true,
  "create_time": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "update_time": "2025-01-20T12:34:56Z"
}

Field Type Label Description market_location_ref MarketLocationRef Official market identifier for this Market Location market_location MarketLocation The logical Market Location (display name, supported directions, time resolution, and user-defined metadata). revision uint64 Monotonically increasing revision counter.

!!! note Each metadata change (e.g., supported_directions, resolution, activation status) increments this counter. ListMarketLocations returns only the latest revision by default. | | is_active | bool | | Whether the Market Location is currently active.

!!! note "Meaning of Activation Status" This flag indicates whether the Market Location is operationally active:

• active = true - New samples MAY be ingested. - The location participates in billing, reconciliation, portfolio aggregation, and trading workflows.

• active = false - No new samples may be ingested. - The location is excluded from operational workflows by default, but: ▪ historical samples remain fully accessible, ▪ historical revisions remain queryable, ▪ reactivation is possible without data loss.

Deactivation represents an administrative state, NOT deletion. It preserves regulatory auditability and long-term metering integrity. | | create_time | google.protobuf.Timestamp | | Timestamp when this Market Location record was first created. | | update_time | google.protobuf.Timestamp | | Timestamp of the most recent metadata change. | | last_deactivated_time | google.protobuf.Timestamp | | Timestamp of the most recent deactivation event.

!!! note Unset when the Market Location has never been deactivated. |

docs.title: MarketLocationId
docs.text:
Market-standard identifier describing a Market Location.

A Market Location is a jurisdiction-specific point of metering used for regulatory processes such as settlement, billing, supplier switching, balancing-group reconciliation, and DSO/TSO reporting. Different markets use incompatible identifier formats—varying in length, character sets, checksum rules, and decomposition.

This message encapsulates the official, market-issued identifier used to reference such a point. Examples: • Germany: MaLo-ID (Marktlokations-ID) • UK: MPAN (Meter Point Administration Number) • US: ESI-ID (Electric Service Identifier) • Australia NMI (National Metering Identifier)

Different markets use incompatible identifier formats—varying in length, character sets, checksum rules, and presentation formatting (spaces, hyphens, prefixes).

!!! example "Example values for different markets" The following examples illustrate how the fields may be populated for different jurisdictions:

| Market:Type     | Official ID         | Normalized Value
| --------------- | ------------------- | -----------------------------
| DE:MALO_ID      | "12345678901"     | "12345678901"
| UK:MPAN         | "18 1066 1234 567 8901 234" | "18106612345678901234"
| US_ERCOT:ESI_ID | "10443720000012345" | "10443720000012345"
| AU:NMI          | "NEM12-03456-A"     | "NEM1203456A"

In each case, `value` preserves the original format as provided by the
market operator, while `normalized_value` is an implementation-specific
cleaned representation suitable for validation, indexing, and
comparisons.
Field Type Label Description id MarketLocationIdValue Official market location identifier. type MarketLocationIdType Identifies what type of official market identifier id represents.

docs.title: MarketLocationIdValue
docs.text:
Opaque identifier in its original market format as received from the source system (MSCONS, DataHub, CSV, manual entry, etc.).

The service accepts both formatted and already-normalized values. Formatting characters (spaces, hyphens, prefixes) are ignored during validation. Validation is performed exclusively on a canonical normalized form derived from the input value, based on the type.

Clients MUST NOT rely on formatting differences to distinguish identifiers.

Examples: - "01234567890" (Germany MaLo) - "18 1066 1234 567 8901 234" (UK MPAN with spaces) - "NEM12-03456-A" (AU NMI with hyphens)

Field Type Label Description value string Official market location identifier.

docs.title: MarketLocationOperationError
docs.text:
Structured error information for a rejected Market Location operation.

This message is present only when the requested operation could not be applied. It provides a machine-readable error code and a human-readable diagnostic message for logging.

Field Type Label Description code MarketLocationOperationErrorCode Machine-readable classification of the failure.

!!! important This field MUST be set when MarketLocationOperationError is present. | | message | string | | Human-readable diagnostic message intended for logging and debugging.

!!! note This field is not guaranteed to be stable and must not be parsed programmatically. |

docs.title: MarketLocationOperationResult
docs.text:
Result of a Market Location lifecycle operation (activate, deactivate, etc.).

Each requested MarketLocationRef yields exactly one result entry. The presence of error determines whether the operation was applied:

Note

• If erroris unset the operation succeeded and mutation occurred. • If erroris set the operation failed and no mutation occurred.

Field Type Label Description market_location_ref MarketLocationRef Market Location on which the operation was requested. update_time google.protobuf.Timestamp Timestamp (UTC) when the operation was successfully applied.

!!! note Populated only when error is unset. | | revision | uint64 | | The new revision of the Market Location after the operation.

!!! note Populated only when error is unset. | | error | MarketLocationOperationError | | Error details describing why the operation was rejected.

!!! note • If unset the operation was applied. • If set the operation was rejected and no mutation occurred. |

docs.title: MarketLocationRef
docs.text:
Identifies a Market Location within a specific enterprise and market area.

This tuple is globally unique across all tenants and combines the owning enterprise with the Market Location selector.

!!! important "Immutability" All fields of MarketLocationRef are immutable once a Market Location has been created. They form the stable, external key used in every RPC that references a Market Location (create, update, activate, deactivate, ingest, stream).

Field Type Label Description enterprise_id uint64 Enterprise id the Market Location belongs to. selector MarketLocationSelector Market Location identity within the enterprise.

docs.title: MarketLocationRevisionSelection
docs.text:
Configuration for selecting which revisions of a Market Location should be returned in a list operation.

Combines the revision strategy (latest vs. all) with an optional filter limiting which historical revisions qualify for inclusion.

Field Type Label Description revision_strategy RevisionStrategy Controls whether only the latest revision or all revisions are returned.

Default: REVISION_STRATEGY_LATEST_ONLY | | changed_fields | MarketLocationChangedField | repeated | Optional filtering of historical revisions by which fields changed.

Example: changed_fields = ["time_resolution", "supported_directions"]

Returned revisions: • rev 1 → always returned (baseline) • rev 2 → returned only if any listed field changed vs rev 1 • rev 3 → returned only if any listed field changed vs rev 2

!!! important • Applied only when revision_strategy = REVISION_STRATEGY_ALL • Ignored otherwise. |

docs.title: MarketLocationSample
docs.text:
Represents a native metering sample submitted via upsert.

Field Type Label Description sample_time google.protobuf.Timestamp Timestamp of the native reading (UTC).

Interpretation depends on the metric type: • ENERGY: start of the interval. • POWER: reference timestamp (instantaneous or averaged). | | value | double | optional | Numeric value measured by the upstream meter.

!!! note "Value for missing samples" When quality = DATA_QUALITY_MISSING, the value SHOULD be unset. | | quality | DataQuality | | Quality classification of the native reading. | | revision | uint64 | | Revision number used to correct previously ingested samples.

Monotonically increasing revision number for the exact tuple: (market_location, direction, metric_type, sample_time)

Larger numbers represent newer revisions. A new revision replaces the previous one only for the same key tuple. |

docs.title: MarketLocationSampleDetail
docs.text:
Represents a metering sample with additional metadata.

This message represents two sample types: 1. Native samples — ingested at the meter’s original resolution. 2. Service-computed samples produced during resampling and/or aggregation.

Field Type Label Description sample_time google.protobuf.Timestamp Timestamp associated with the sample. value double optional The numeric value, if available.

!!! note "Missing value" This may be unset in the case the native reading was missing when quality = MISSING or if no native samples were present for the resampling window. | | quality | DataQuality | | Quality classification of the sample.

For native samples this reflects the meter-provided quality. For resampled values this reflects the semantic quality of the aggregate. | | revision | uint64 | optional | Revision number for native samples.

!!! note "Missing revision" For resampled values, this field is unset in case resampling combined multiple samples with different revisions. | | sample_update_time | google.protobuf.Timestamp | | Timestamp when the sample was last updated.

!!! note "Timestamp interpretation" For native samples this represents the ingestion timestamp while for resampled values this indicates when the service computed the resampled interval window. | | resampling_method | ResamplingMethod | | How this sample was produced: native, downsampled, upsampled. |

docs.title: MarketLocationSamplesStreamFilter
docs.text:
General filter criteria for querying samples uniformly apply to all Market Locations, directions, and metric types in this request.

Field Type Label Description resampling_options ResamplingOptions Optional resampling options like resolution for the data, represented in seconds. If omitted, samples are returned at their original stored, native resolution.

!!! note "Missing native samples" If a resampling interval contains no native samples, the service emits a sample with its value unset. | | revision_strategy | RevisionStrategy | | Optional revision-selection strategy applied when multiple revisions exist for the same timestamp. If unspecified defaults to the latest revision. For samples, the highest numeric revision value represents the newest version.

Example: timestamp = 2025-01-01T00:00Z revisions: • rev 1 (MEASURED) • rev 2 (CORRECTED) • rev 3 (CORRECTED)

  • LATEST_ONLY → selects only rev 3 - ALL → selects rev 1, rev 2, rev 3

!!! important "Effect on Resampling" When resampling is enabled, revision_strategy only determines which native revisions contribute to the aggregate, but the output always contains exactly one sample per interval. Late-arriving native samples may trigger corrected resampled values for past intervals. | | time_filter | TimeFilter | | Optional Time-filter defining the historical window and real-time behaviour of the stream.

Semantics: • If end_time is provided, it MUST be ≤ the current server time. The server streams all samples t where start_time ≤ t < end_time and then closes the stream.

• If end_time is omitted, the server streams all historical samples t ≥ start_time (if provided) and then continues streaming new samples in real time. The stream remains open indefinitely.

• If start_time is omitted: – and end_time is omitted: the stream produces no historical data and begins streaming real-time samples only. – and end_time is provided: the historical window is empty and the stream closes immediately. |

docs.title: MarketLocationSelector
docs.text:
Identifies a Market Location within the clients enterprise scope.

This selector does not contain an enterprise_id. The target enterprise is derived from the client's authorized enterprise scope.

Field Type Label Description market_area MarketArea Regulatory jurisdiction in which this Market Location is registered. market_location_id MarketLocationId Official market identifier (MaLo-ID, MPAN, ESI-ID, ...).

docs.title: MarketLocationSeries
docs.text:
Represents a semantic time series for a single logical Market Location.

Field Type Label Description market_location_ref MarketLocationRef The market location to which this sample belongs. direction EnergyFlowDirection Energy-flow direction of this series (IMPORT or EXPORT). Derived from the request and validated against supported_directions. metric_type MetricType Metric type represented by this series (e.g., ENERGY, POWER). metric_unit MetricUnit The physical unit in which the metric is expressed (e.g., kWh, kW, kVArh). resolution TimeResolution Market Location's current contractual resolution. samples MarketLocationSampleDetail repeated Ordered samples representing this semantic time series.

docs.title: MarketLocationsFilter
docs.text:
Filters for selecting market locations.

A Market Location must match all specified criteria to be included in the result.

!!! note "Filter Semantics" • Each repeated field (e.g., market_location_id_filters) is evaluated using logical OR. • Different filter fields (if more are added in the future) will be combined using logical AND. • If no filters are provided, all Market Locations of the enterprise are returned.

Field Type Label Description market_location_id_filters MarketLocationIdValue repeated Optional filter to match one or more Market Locations by their official ID. activation_filter ActivationFilter Optional filter for which activation states to include.

!!! note "Default Behavior" By default, only active Market Locations are returned. |

docs.title: ReceiveMarketLocationSamplesStreamRequest
docs.text:
Request for streaming time-series samples for one or more logical Market Locations.

!!! note "Sample Series Expansion Logic" The server creates one independent time series for every unique combination of: • MarketLocationRef • EnergyFlowDirection • MetricType

Example:
    2 Market Locations × 1 Direction × 2 Metrics = 4 series

Each of these is emitted as a separate MarketLocationSeries in the
streamed response.

!!! example "Example Request" The following example requests ENERGY samples for two Market Locations, both in IMPORT direction, over a 24-hour window:

```json
{
  "market_location_refs": [
    {
      "enterprise_id": 42,
      "market_location_id": {
        "value": "DE01234567890",
        "type": "MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_MALO_ID"
      }
    },
    {
      "enterprise_id": 44,
      "market_location_id": {
        "value": "18 1066 1234 567 8901 234",
        "type": "MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_MPAN"
      }
    }
  ],
  "directions": [
    "ENERGY_FLOW_DIRECTION_IMPORT"
  ],
  "metric_types": [
    "METRIC_TYPE_ACTIVE_ENERGY"
  ],
  "stream_filter": {
    "revision_strategy": "REVISION_STRATEGY_LATEST_ONLY",
    "time_filter": {
      "interval": {
        "start_time": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "end_time":   "2025-01-02T00:00:00Z"
      }
    },
    "resampling_options": {
      "resolution": "TIME_RESOLUTION_15_MIN"
    }
  }
}
```
Field Type Label Description market_locations MarketLocationSelector repeated A list of Market Location`s to receive samples for. directions EnergyFlowDirection repeated Energy-flow directions requested (e.g., IMPORT and/or EXPORT).

Clients may specify one or multiple directions. If multiple directions are provided, the server expands them into separate time series. | | metric_types | MetricType | repeated | Requested metric types (e.g., ENERGY, POWER).

At least one metric type must be provided. The server produces one series per (market_location × direction × metric_type) tuple. | | stream_filter | MarketLocationSamplesStreamFilter | | Global stream-level filter applied to all returned series. |

docs.title: ReceiveMarketLocationSamplesStreamResponse
docs.text:
Streaming response containing one or more time series fragments.

The service emits a distinct MarketLocationSeries message for every unique tuple of Market Location, EnergyFlowDirection and MetricType.

The RPC is a finite server-side stream: once all samples matching the request (across all Market Locations, directions, and metric types) have been delivered, the server closes the stream. However, if the request’s time_filter specifies no end_time, the stream continues in real time.

Consumers should treat each market location series in each streamed message as an independent, self-contained segment. Responses may be chunked.

!!! note "Incremental / Chunked Streaming" The service may emit: • complete series in a single message, or • multiple incremental/chunked segments.

!!! note "Sample Ordering & Updates" There is no guaranteed ordering between different series, between chunks of different series, or across series. A client MUST treat every received MarketLocationSeries as an independent, self-contained segment and merge or sort samples locally if ordering is required.

The service may also emit more than one sample with identical
`sample_time`. This is normal and reflects the correction workflows
required in regulated metering and real-time resampling.

A sample may be re-emitted whenever the service obtains better or newer
information for that timestamp—whether through revised native readings,
delayed arrivals, or updated resampling intervals.

Clients MUST deduplicate samples for the same `sample_time` by:

  1. Prefer the sample with the highest revision, when revisions
     are present, otherwise
  2. Prefer the sample with the latest update_time.

This rule applies uniformly to both native and resampled streams.

!!! example "Example Response Fragment" Below is an example fragment of a streamed response for a request that queried IMPORT active energy values for a single Market Location over a 24-hour period (no downsampling or upsampling applied).

```json
{
  "time_filter": {
    "interval": {
      "start_time": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "end_time":   "2025-01-02T00:00:00Z"
    }
  },
  "revision_strategy": "REVISION_STRATEGY_LATEST_ONLY",
  "resampling_options": {
    "resolution": "TIME_RESOLUTION_15_MIN",
    "downsampling_method": "DOWNSAMPLING_METHOD_MEAN"
  },
  "series": [
    {
      "market_location_ref": {
        "enterprise_id": 42,
        "market_location_id": {
          "value": "DE01234567890",
          "type": "MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_MALO_ID"
        }
      },
      "direction": "ENERGY_FLOW_DIRECTION_IMPORT",
      "metric_type": "METRIC_TYPE_ACTIVE_ENERGY",
      "metric_unit": "METRIC_UNIT_KWH",
      "resolution": "TIME_RESOLUTION_15_MIN",
      "samples": [
        {
          "sample_time": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
          "value": 1.234,
          "quality": "DATA_QUALITY_MEASURED",
          "revision": 1,
          "sample_update_time": "2025-01-01T00:00:02Z",
          "resampling_method": "RESAMPLING_METHOD_NATIVE"
        },
        {
          "sample_time": "2025-01-01T00:15:00Z",
          "value": 0.987,
          "quality": "DATA_QUALITY_MEASURED",
          "revision": 1,
          "sample_update_time": "2025-01-01T00:15:02Z",
          "resampling_method": "RESAMPLING_METHOD_NATIVE"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
Field Type Label Description stream_filter MarketLocationSamplesStreamFilter Echoes the request's stream filter for client convenience. series MarketLocationSeries repeated List of market location metering time series included in this fragment.

docs.title: ResamplingOptions
docs.text:
Resampling options for Market Location time-series data.

Resampling allows clients to request a time resolution that differs from the Market Location’s native stored resolution. The service constructs a uniform output grid based on the requested resolution and produces exactly one sample per interval.

Two semantic modes may result:

• Downsampling (when the requested resolution is coarser) Multiple native samples fall into one output interval; these are combined using the selected aggregation method.

• Upsampling (when the requested resolution is finer) Each native sample expands into multiple sub-intervals. ENERGY is allocated proportionally, while POWER is repeated stepwise.

In both cases the output sample timestamp equals the start of the interval in the materialized grid.

!!! example "Example: Downsampling from 1-minute to 15-minute intervals" The stored time series has a native resolution of Δt = 1 minute. Resampling is requested with a resolution of ΔT = 15 minutes. In this case all native samples whose timestamps fall within an interval [t, t + Δt) contribute to the aggregated value for that interval. The timestamp of the aggregated sample is exactly t, the start of the interval.

For each interval k:
    Ik = [T0 + k·ΔT,  T0 + (k+1)·ΔT)

The aggregated value A_k is the arithmetic mean of all samples whose
timestamps ts satisfy: ts ∈ Ik

The resampled series consists of points:
    (t = T0 + k·ΔT,  value = A_k)

!!! example "Upsampling: 15-minute → 5-minute" If the native resolution is Δt = 15 min and the requested resolution is ΔT = 5 min, each native interval expands into three equally sized sub-intervals, with ENERGY proportionally allocated and POWER repeated.

Field Type Label Description resolution TimeResolution Optional resampling resolution for the output time series. downsampling_method DownsamplingMethod Optional aggregation method applied when downsampling. Defaults to DOWNSAMPLING_METHOD_MEAN when omitted.

docs.title: SampleUpsertError
docs.text:
Structured error information for a rejected sample upsert.

A SampleUpsertError describes why a sample could not be inserted or updated. It provides both a machine-readable classification and optional diagnostic information to support reconciliation and retry logic.

!!! note "Error presence semantics" This message is present only when the upsert was rejected.

Field Type Label Description error_code SampleUpsertErrorCode Machine-readable classification of a failure. error_message string Optional human-readable diagnostic message intended for logging and debugging. existing_sample MarketLocationSampleDetail The stored sample that prevented this upsert.

Populated only when the service can identify an existing stored sample for the same tuple:

(market_location_ref, direction, metric_type, metric_unit, sample_time)

Behavior by error_code:

• REVISION_CONFLICT A sample with the same revision already exists but differs in payload. The returned sample has the same revision number.

• REVISION_TOO_OLD A newer revision already exists. The returned sample represents the latest stored revision (highest numeric revision).

• Other error codes This field is unset.

!!! important existing_sample always refers to the same logical tuple as the request. It never refers to a different timestamp or metric. |

docs.title: TimeFilter
docs.text:
Filters records by a UTC time interval.

A metering sample represents a measured value for a fixed-resolution interval (e.g., 15 minutes). This filter restricts the returned samples to those whose interval start timestamps fall within an optional time window.

The time window is inclusive at the start and exclusive at the end: start_time ≤ sample_timestamp < end_time>

!!! note "Filter Logic" - interval is optional; if omitted, all timestamps are matched. - Only sample timestamps within the interval are included. - Interval semantics follow ISO 8601 conventions and match those used by other Frequenz services.

!!! example "Example: All samples on or after a timestamp" 

{
  "interval": {
    "start_time": "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
}

!!! example "Example: Samples in a closed-open time window" 

{
  "interval": {
    "start_time": "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z",
    "end_time":   "2025-06-02T00:00:00Z"
  }
}

Field Type Label Description interval frequenz.api.common.v1alpha8.types.Interval Optional; Time window for matching sample interval start timestamps.

If omitted, samples from all timestamps are included. |

docs.title: UpdateMarketLocationRequest
docs.text:
Updates metadata of an existing Market Location.

Only a restricted subset of Market Location metadata may be updated. These rules preserve regulatory auditability and prevent retroactive changes that would conflict with historical billing, settlement, or reconciliation processes.

Updates always produce a new metadata revision. Historical revisions remain retrievable when using revision_strategy = REVISION_STRATEGY_ALL.

Field Type Label Description market_location_selector MarketLocationSelector Identifies the Market Location being updated. expected_revision uint64 The revision the caller expects to be the latest revision at the time this update is applied.

This field prevents lost updates when multiple callers update the same Market Location concurrently. Callers should first read the latest MarketLocationDetail, then pass its revision here. On mismatch, the service returns with an error indicating the current latest revision. | | update_mask | google.protobuf.FieldMask | | Field mask specifying which fields inside update_fields should be applied.

Allowed field mask paths: "display_name" "supported_directions" "time_resolution" "payload"

Attempts to reference immutable fields result in INVALID_ARGUMENT. | | update_fields | UpdateMarketLocationRequest.MarketLocationUpdate | | Values to apply to the fields listed in update_mask. |

docs.title: UpdateMarketLocationRequest.MarketLocationUpdate
docs.text:
Container for all mutable Market Location fields.

!!! important "Metadata Updates" The following fields are mutable:

  • display_name
  • payload

The following fields are conditionally mutable:

  • supported_directions
      - Append-only: new directions may be added.
        Example: [IMPORT] → [IMPORT, EXPORT]
      - Removing directions is NOT allowed because historical samples
        may exist for those directions.

  • time_resolution
      - May be updated only to a finer resolution (e.g., PT60M →
        PT15M).
      - Resolution changes apply only to future samples; historical
        samples retain their original resolution.
Field Type Label Description display_name string Optional human-readable name for organizational or UI use. supported_directions EnergyFlowDirection repeated Supported energy-flow directions.

!!! note "Allowed Modifications" • Directions may be added (IMPORT → IMPORT+EXPORT) • Directions may NOT be removed. | | time_resolution | TimeResolution | | Primary contractual time resolution (e.g., PT15M, PT30M).

!!! note "Allowed Modifications" • May only change to a finer resolution. • Example: PT60M → PT15M is allowed; PT15M → PT60M is not. | | payload | google.protobuf.Struct | | Optional user-defined structured metadata. |

docs.title: UpdateMarketLocationResponse
docs.text:
Response returned after updating a Market Location.

The response always contains the latest revision of the Market Location after the update has been applied. Historical revisions remain retrievable using revision-aware listing operations.

!!! note "Revision Behavior" Every successful update creates a new metadata revision. Revision numbers increase monotonically and allow clients to:

  • detect configuration drift,
  • reconcile state across microservices,
  • audit changes over time.

!!! example "Example Response" 

{
  "enterprise_id": 42,
  "market_location_detail": {
    "market_location_ref": {
      "enterprise_id": 42,
      "market_area": "MARKET_AREA_EU_DE",
      "market_location_id": {
        "value": "DE01234567890",
        "type": "MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_MALO_ID"
      }
    },
    "market_location": {
      "display_name": "Main Office – Updated",
      "supported_directions": [
        "ENERGY_FLOW_DIRECTION_IMPORT",
        "ENERGY_FLOW_DIRECTION_EXPORT"
      ],
      "time_resolution": "TIME_RESOLUTION_15_MIN",
      "payload": {
        "site_type": "retail",
        "owner": "ACME Energy"
      }
    },
    "revision": 4,
    "is_active": true,
    "create_time": "2024-12-01T10:00:00Z",
    "update_time": "2025-01-15T08:30:00Z"
  }
}

Field Type Label Description enterprise_id uint64 Enterprise that owns the Market Location. market_location_detail MarketLocationDetail Updated Market Location metadata, including: • new revision number, • updated fields, • activation status, • timestamps.

docs.title: UpsertMarketLocationSamplesStreamRequest
docs.text:
A single ingestion event for one Market Location sample.

Each request message processes exactly one sample and produces one acknowledgement response.

The server performs strict validation of: • timestamp alignment with the Market Location's contractual resolution, • energy-flow direction against supported_directions, • metric_type against supported metrics, • metric_unit consistency with metric_type, • revision monotonicity for the (ML, direction, metric, timestamp) tuple.

!!! important "Correction via revisioning (no deletion)" The MarketMeteringService never deletes samples. Regulated metering processes require a full historical audit trail.

A previously ingested sample is corrected by submitting a new revision
with the same sample_time but a higher revision value.

Typical patterns:
  • Invalidate a value → send a new revision with
    `quality = DATA_QUALITY_MISSING` and value = 0.
  • Correct a value    → send a new revision with the corrected value
    and `quality = DATA_QUALITY_CORRECTED`.

The backend selects the highest revision when serving data, while older
revisions remain queryable via revision strategies.

!!! warning "Timestamp alignment is mandatory" sample.sample_time MUST align with the Market Location's contractual time_resolution.

Example:
  time_resolution = PT15M → allowed times are:
    00:00, 00:15, 00:30, 00:45, ...

Misaligned timestamps are rejected. By default, the service rejects
samples whose `sample_time` is in the future relative to the server
clock and may also reject samples that are too far in the past.

!!! warning "Metric-unit consistency is validated" The provided metric_unit MUST be compatible with metric_type. ENERGY → {Wh, kWh, MWh} POWER → {W, kW, MW} REACTIVE_ENERGY → {VArh, kVArh, MVArh} REACTIVE_POWER → {VAr, kVAr, MVAr}

The backend does not perform unit conversion.

!!! warning "Direction and metric must be allowed" direction MUST be present in the Market Location's supported_directions. metric_type MUST be supported for ingestion by the service.

Field Type Label Description market_location MarketLocationSelector Identifies the target Market Location. direction EnergyFlowDirection Energy-flow direction (IMPORT or EXPORT).

MUST match one of the Market Location's supported_directions, or the request is rejected. | | metric_type | MetricType | | The metric type being ingested (e.g., ENERGY, POWER).

MUST be consistent with metric_unit below. | | metric_unit | MetricUnit | | The physical unit of the value (e.g., kWh, kW).

MUST be coherent with metric_type; no implicit unit conversion occurs. | | sample | MarketLocationSample | | Sample data, including sample_time, value, quality, and revision.

sample.sample_time MUST: • be in UTC, • align with the Market Location time_resolution, • be within the service's allowed ingestion window. |

docs.title: UpsertMarketLocationSamplesStreamResponse
docs.text:
Acknowledgement for a single sample upsert operation.

Each request message produces exactly one response message. The response ALWAYS echoes the attempted input sample, regardless of whether the operation succeeded or was rejected.

The presence of error determines whether the upsert was accepted:

• error unset → the sample was accepted (inserted or recognized as an idempotent no-op). • error set → the sample was rejected.

!!! note "Echo semantics" The sample field always represents the client-submitted payload. It does NOT reflect server-side canonicalization or stored metadata. In particular, server-assigned timestamps (e.g. ingest_time) are returned separately.

Field Type Label Description market_location_ref MarketLocationRef The Market Location to which this sample belongs (echoed from request). direction EnergyFlowDirection Energy-flow direction of the sample (echoed from request). metric_type MetricType Metric type of the sample (echoed from request). metric_unit MetricUnit Metric unit of the sample (echoed from request). sample MarketLocationSample Echo of the client-submitted sample.

!!! note This field is populated even when ingestion fails. It represents the attempted input—not the stored record. On success, its content will match the stored sample except for server-generated metadata. | | ingest_time | google.protobuf.Timestamp | | Timestamp (UTC) when the sample was successfully processed by the service.

!!! note • Populated only when error is unset. • Assigned by the service and may differ from client clock time. • Represents ingestion/acceptance time, not sample.sample_time. | | error | SampleUpsertError | | Optional error details. If set, the upsert was rejected.

!!! note • If unset the upsert was accepted. • If set the upsert was rejected and no mutation occurred. |

docs.title: ActivationFilter
docs.text:
Activation-state filter for Market Locations.

!!! note "Safe default" If unspecified, the service returns only active Market Locations.

This avoids accidentally including inactive Market Locations in workflows such as trading, billing, or operational automation.

Name Number Description ACTIVATION_FILTER_UNSPECIFIED 0 UNSPECIFIED: Defaults to ONLY_ACTIVE. ACTIVATION_FILTER_ONLY_ACTIVE 1 ONLY_ACTIVE: Return only active Market Locations. ACTIVATION_FILTER_ONLY_INACTIVE 2 ONLY_INACTIVE: Return only inactive Market Locations. ACTIVATION_FILTER_ALL 3 ALL: Return both active and inactive Market Locations.

docs.title: DataQuality
docs.text:
Classification of data quality for a metering sample.

Many regulated markets deliver values that may be measured, estimated, corrected, or intentionally flagged as missing. This enum provides a normalized representation of these states.

Name Number Description DATA_QUALITY_UNSPECIFIED 0 UNSPECIFIED: Default value — should not occur in valid data. DATA_QUALITY_MEASURED 1 MEASURED: Raw value directly received from the metering system or DSO. Represents an original, unmodified reading. DATA_QUALITY_ESTIMATED 2 ESTIMATED: Value inferred or interpolated due to missing or invalid meter readings (e.g., outages, communication gaps, profile-based estimation). Indicates reduced accuracy compared to a measured value. DATA_QUALITY_CORRECTED 3 CORRECTED: Value that was initially delivered but later amended during validation, reconciliation, or settlement processes (e.g., corrections, plausibility adjustments, manual review). DATA_QUALITY_MISSING 4 MISSING: No valid value is available for this interval.

docs.title: DownsamplingMethod
docs.text:
Defines how multiple native samples are combined when downsampling to a coarser resolution.

Name Number Description DOWNSAMPLING_METHOD_UNSPECIFIED 0 UNSPECIFIED: Defaults to MEAN. DOWNSAMPLING_METHOD_MEAN 1 MEAN: Arithmetic mean of all samples within the interval.

docs.title: EnergyFlowDirection
docs.text:
Describes the direction of energy flow for metering samples.

This is used in data queries and ingestion to select the correct "side" of a Market Location. For example, in Germany there are separate Market Locations for import and export. In other markets (e.g. UK, US) a single identifier may be bidirectional.

Name Number Description ENERGY_FLOW_DIRECTION_UNSPECIFIED 0 UNSPECIFIED: Default unspecified value — must not be used. ENERGY_FLOW_DIRECTION_IMPORT 1 Energy flowing from grid to customer (consumption). ENERGY_FLOW_DIRECTION_EXPORT 2 Energy flowing from customer to grid (generation / feed-in).

docs.title: MarketArea
docs.text:
Defines the jurisdiction in which a Market Location is registered.

A Market Area represents the regulatory jurisdiction and market regime that governs identifier formats, settlement periods, and metering conventions for a Market Location.

Identifier formats (MaLo-ID, MPAN, POD, NMI, ESI-ID, …) are modeled separately in MarketLocationIdType.

!!! note "Jurisdictions, not operators" Market areas represent regulatory regimes, not individual exchanges or TSOs. Where operator-specific behavior matters (e.g. ERCOT vs PJM), dedicated sub-areas are defined.

!!! note "Numeric ranges" Enum values are grouped by region to preserve ordering, readability, and backwards-compatible extension.

Name Number Description MARKET_AREA_UNSPECIFIED 0 UNSPECIFIED: Default unspecified value — must not be used. MARKET_AREA_EU_DE 101 EU_DE: Germany — MaLo-ID regime (Marktlokation / MaLo-ID). MARKET_AREA_EU_UK 102 EU_UK: United Kingdom — MPAN regime (Meter Point Administration Number). MARKET_AREA_EU_FR 103 EU_FR: France — PDL/PRM regime (Point de Livraison/Référence Mesure). MARKET_AREA_EU_IT 104 EU_IT: Italy — POD regime (Point of Delivery). MARKET_AREA_EU_ES 105 EU_ES: Spain — CUPS regime (Código Universal de Punto de Suministro). MARKET_AREA_EU_NL 106 EU_NL: Netherlands — EAN regime (European Article Number). MARKET_AREA_EU_BE 107 EU_BE: Belgium — EAN regime. MARKET_AREA_EU_CH 108 EU_CH: Switzerland — EAN regime. MARKET_AREA_EU_AT 109 EU_AT: Austria — Zählpunktnummer (EAN-based). MARKET_AREA_EU_NORDICS 110 EU_NORDICS: Nordic region — Elhub / GSRN regime (NO, SE, DK, FI). MARKET_AREA_AP_JP 201 AP_JP: Japan — country-specific metering / settlement regime. MARKET_AREA_AP_CN 202 AP_CN: China — country-specific metering / settlement regime. MARKET_AREA_AP_IN 203 AP_IN: India — country-specific metering / settlement regime. MARKET_AREA_AP_SG 204 AP_SG: Singapore — country-specific metering / settlement regime. MARKET_AREA_NA_US_ERCOT 301 NA_US_ERCOT: United States — ERCOT regime (ESI-ID). MARKET_AREA_NA_US_PJM 302 NA_US_PJM: United States — PJM regime (ESI-ID). MARKET_AREA_NA_US_ISONE 303 NA_US_ISONE: United States — ISO New England regime (ESI-ID). MARKET_AREA_NA_US_CAISO 304 NA_US_CAISO: United States — CAISO regime (ESI-ID). MARKET_AREA_EURASIA_RU 401 EURASIA_RU: Russia — country-specific metering / settlement regime. MARKET_AREA_OC_AU 501 OC_AU: Australia — NMI regime (National Metering Identifier). MARKET_AREA_OC_NZ 502 OC_NZ: New Zealand — ICP regime (Installation Control Point). MARKET_AREA_OTHER 999 OTHER: Other or not yet modelled areas.

docs.title: MarketLocationChangedField
docs.text:
Indicates which fields of a Market Location changed in this revision.

A revision may reflect one or many changed fields. The enum is intentionally coarse-grained to mirror the update semantics.

Note

If new updatable fields are added to MarketLocationUpdate in the future, a corresponding enum value should be added here.

Name Number Description MARKET_LOCATION_CHANGED_FIELD_UNSPECIFIED 0 UNSPECIFIED: Should not be used in valid responses. MARKET_LOCATION_CHANGED_FIELD_SUPPORTED_DIRECTIONS 1 SUPPORTED DIRECTIONS: Supported import/export directions changed. MARKET_LOCATION_CHANGED_FIELD_TIME_RESOLUTION 2 TIME RESOLUTION: Contractual time resolution changed. MARKET_LOCATION_CHANGED_FIELD_IS_ACTIVE 3 IS_ACTIVE: Activation status changed (activate/deactivate).

docs.title: MarketLocationIdType
docs.text:
Identifies the type of external market identifier used to reference a Market Location in a specific regulatory regime.

The identifier type defines the format, validation rules, and semantics of the identifier value. Jurisdictional applicability is modeled separately via MarketArea.

!!! note "Identifier regimes, not countries" Some identifier types (e.g. EAN, ESI_ID) are used across multiple jurisdictions. This enum models identifier formats, not geography.

Name Number Description MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED 0 UNSPECIFIED: Default unspecified value — must not be used. MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_MALO_ID 1 MALO_ID: Germany – Marktlokations-ID (MaLo-ID). MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_ZAEHLPUNKT 2 ZAEHLPUNKT: Austria – Zählpunktbezeichnung (Semantically similar to Germany’s MaLo-ID). MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_MPAN 3 MPAN: United Kingdom – Meter Point Administration Number. MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_POD 4 POD: Italy — Point of Delivery. MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_CUPS 5 CUPS: Spain — Código Universal de Punto de Suministro. MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_PRM 6 PRM: France — Point de Référence et Mesure (PRM). MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_EAN 7 EAN: Continental Europe (e.g. FR (legacy), NL, BE, PL, CZ, HU, ...) — European Article Number. MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_GSRN 8 GSRN: Nordic countries (e.g., DK, SE, NO, FI) — GS1 Global Service Relation Number. MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_ESI_ID 9 ESI_ID: United States – Electric Service Identifier. MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_NMI 10 NMI: Australia – National Metering Identifier. MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_ICP 11 ICP: New Zealand — Installation Control Point. MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_SPN 12 SPN: Japan — Supply Point Number (需要地点特定番号). MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_OTHER 99 OTHER: Generic meter identifier for markets not modeled explicitly yet.

docs.title: MarketLocationOperationErrorCode
docs.text:
Classification of structured error conditions that may occur when activating or deactivating a Market Location.

Name Number Description MARKET_LOCATION_OPERATION_ERROR_CODE_UNSPECIFIED 0 UNSPECIFIED: Should not be used in valid responses. MARKET_LOCATION_OPERATION_ERROR_CODE_NOT_FOUND 1 NOT_FOUND: The Market Location could not be found within the specified enterprise. MARKET_LOCATION_OPERATION_ERROR_CODE_ALREADY_IN_TARGET_STATE 2 ALREADY_IN_TARGET_STATE: The caller attempted to activate/deactivate a Market Location that is already in the desired state. MARKET_LOCATION_OPERATION_ERROR_CODE_ENTERPRISE_MISMATCH 3 ENTERPRISE_MISMATCH: The provided market location id references an enterprise that does not match the enterprise of the stored Market Location. MARKET_LOCATION_OPERATION_ERROR_CODE_PERMISSION_DENIED 4 PERMISSION_DENIED: The caller is not authorized to mutate this Market Location. MARKET_LOCATION_OPERATION_ERROR_CODE_OPERATION_REJECTED 5 OPERATION_REJECTED: A service validation rule or invariant prevented the operation. MARKET_LOCATION_OPERATION_ERROR_CODE_UNKNOWN_ERROR 99 UNKNOWN_ERROR: Any other unexpected service-side error.

docs.title: MetricType
docs.text:
Defines the fundamental physical property being measured.

docs.title: MetricUnit
docs.text:
Defines the unit of measurement for a sample value.

Name Number Description METRIC_UNIT_UNSPECIFIED 0 UNSPECIFIED: Default value — should not appear in valid data. METRIC_UNIT_WH 1 Watt-hour (Wh): Small-scale active energy unit. Typically used for fine-granularity registers or device-level measurement. METRIC_UNIT_KWH 2 Kilowatt-hour (kWh): Standard billing and settlement unit for active energy in most global markets (DE, UK, AU, US, etc.). METRIC_UNIT_MWH 3 Megawatt-hour (MWh): Large-scale active energy unit, commonly used in wholesale markets, trading, and TSO reporting. METRIC_UNIT_W 10 Watt (W): Base SI unit for active power. Often used for device telemetry or short-duration calculations. METRIC_UNIT_KW 11 Kilowatt (kW): Standard unit for instantaneous or averaged active power in commercial and industrial metering. METRIC_UNIT_MW 12 Megawatt (MW): Unit for large-scale power flows used in wholesale trading, balancing, and TSO/ISO operational systems. METRIC_UNIT_VARH 20 Volt-ampere-reactive-hour (VArh): Small-scale reactive energy unit, rarely used outside technical diagnostics. METRIC_UNIT_KVARH 21 Kilovolt-ampere-reactive-hour (kVArh): Standard settlement unit in jurisdictions that bill for reactive energy. METRIC_UNIT_MVARH 22 Megavolt-ampere-reactive-hour (MVArh): Used in high-voltage or transmission-level reactive accounting. METRIC_UNIT_VAR 30 Volt-ampere-reactive (VAr): Base unit for instantaneous reactive power. METRIC_UNIT_KVAR 31 Kilovolt-ampere-reactive (kVAr): Standard unit for reactive power in distribution networks and large commercial installations. METRIC_UNIT_MVAR 32 Megavolt-ampere-reactive (MVAr): Used in transmission-level system management and reactive capability reporting.

docs.title: ResamplingMethod
docs.text:
Indicates how a returned sample was derived relative to the originally stored metering resolution.

Name Number Description RESAMPLING_METHOD_UNSPECIFIED 0 UNSPECIFIED: Default — should not appear in valid API responses. RESAMPLING_METHOD_NATIVE 1 NATIVE: The sample is stored at this exact resolution in the backend. RESAMPLING_METHOD_DOWNSAMPLED 2 DOWNSAMPLED: The sample is computed from finer-granularity data. Example: native = 1 min; requested = 15 min. RESAMPLING_METHOD_UPSAMPLED 3 UPSAMPLED: The sample is computed from coarser-granularity data. Example: native = 15 min; requested = 5 min.

!!! important Upsampling cannot create new information. Values are typically distributed (for energy) or repeated/interpolated (for power). |

docs.title: RevisionStrategy
docs.text:
Strategy for selecting which revisions of a resource should be returned.

Many entities in regulated energy systems evolve over time and may exist in multiple historical revisions. Examples include: • time-series samples that receive corrections or late updates • Market Location metadata updated by the user or backend processes

This enum allows clients to control whether they want only the most recent version of each entity or the full revision history.

!!! note "Revision ordering" Revisions are ordered strictly by their numeric revision field. The service does not infer semantics from market-specific document types or timestamps — the highest numeric revision always represents the newest version of a given entity.

Name Number Description REVISION_STRATEGY_UNSPECIFIED 0 UNSPECIFIED: Should not be used. Defaults to LATEST_ONLY. REVISION_STRATEGY_LATEST_ONLY 1 LATEST_ONLY: Return only the newest revision of each entity.

!!! note The newest revision is determined solely by the highest numeric revision value. | | REVISION_STRATEGY_ALL | 2 | ALL: Return every available revision of each entity.

!!! note Consumers must handle multiple entries representing the same logical entity or timestamp, differentiated only by revision number. |

docs.title: TimeResolution
docs.text:
Defines the time resolution (sampling interval) of metering data.

All timestamps refer to the start of the measured interval, and the interval runs until: [timestamp, timestamp + resolution)

Resolutions are modeled explicitly because different markets use different fixed intervals.

!!! example "Common resolution examples" These intervals are commonly encountered in interval metering systems worldwide:

| Jurisdiction        | Metric Type      | Resolution
|---------------------|------------------|------------
| Germany (MaLo)      | Energy (kWh)     | PT15M
| UK (MPAN)           | Energy (kWh)     | PT30M
| Australia (NEM12)   | Energy (Wh)      | PT5M
| US (ERCOT)          | Power (kW)       | PT5M
| US (PJM/ISO-NE)     | Power/Energy     | PT1H
| Smart meters (AMI)  | Energy           | PT1M

!!! note "Primary Resolution" A Market Location typically has one primary contractual resolution. Some systems may support additional resolutions (e.g., for telemetry or submetering).

Name Number Description TIME_RESOLUTION_UNSPECIFIED 0 UNSPECIFIED: Must not be used. TIME_RESOLUTION_1_MIN 1 PT1M: 1-minute interval. Used in some modern AMI systems (US, AU) and for high-frequency metering. TIME_RESOLUTION_2_MIN 2 PT2M: 2-minute interval. Rare, but supported by some industrial submetering systems. TIME_RESOLUTION_5_MIN 3 PT5M: 5-minute interval. Used in Australia (AEMO NEM12), US ISOs (ERCOT), and many AMI systems. TIME_RESOLUTION_10_MIN 4 PT10M: 10-minute interval. Seen in some Asian and utility-specific formats. TIME_RESOLUTION_15_MIN 5 PT15M: 15-minute interval. Standard for Germany (MSCONS), Switzerland, Italy, Netherlands, and future Nordic harmonization. TIME_RESOLUTION_30_MIN 6 PT30M: 30-minute interval. Historic UK settlement period; still widely used for MPAN half-hourly data. TIME_RESOLUTION_60_MIN 7 PT60M: 60-minute interval (1 hour). Nordic ElHub standard; common in US and Canadian utilities. TIME_RESOLUTION_1_DAY 8 P1D: Daily resolution. Used for coarse-granularity reporting or legacy billing schemas.

docs.title: MarketMeteringService
docs.text:
Metering data ingestion is performed using the bidirectional stream Each message carries a single metering value together with its metadata, and corrections are applied by submitting a new sample for the same timestamp and a higher revision. The service never deletes or overwrites earlier revisions; instead, each correction creates an immutable audit trail.

5. Retrieve historical and real-time metering data

   Depending on the time filter, the service may return a finite
   historical dataset, continue seamlessly into real-time mode once
   historical samples are exhausted, or stream only real-time
   measurements if no start_time is provided. Optional resampling
   may be applied to request coarser intervals; in this mode,
   late-arriving native samples can trigger corrected resampled
   outputs for previously emitted windows.

Together, these operations form a complete lifecycle for managing,
correcting, and streaming billing-grade metering data across global
electricity markets.

!!! important "Authentication" All requests to MarketMeteringService must be signed. The key identifier and signature must be included in the request metadata (gRPC metadata / HTTP headers). The signature must be computed using the HMAC-SHA256 algorithm and secret key. All requests to this service must be made over TLS (HTTPS).

Defines the jurisdiction in which a Market Location is registered.

A Market Area represents the regulatory jurisdiction and market regime that governs identifier formats, settlement periods, and metering conventions for a Market Location.

Identifier formats (MaLo-ID, MPAN, POD, NMI, ESI-ID, …) are modeled separately in MarketLocationIdType.

Jurisdictions, not operators

Market areas represent regulatory regimes, not individual exchanges or TSOs. Where operator-specific behavior matters (e.g. ERCOT vs PJM), dedicated sub-areas are defined.

Numeric ranges

Enum values are grouped by region to preserve ordering, readability, and backwards-compatible extension.

docs.title: frequenz.api.marketmetering.v1alpha1.marketmetering_pb2.MarketLocation
docs.text:
Bases: Message

Represents a logical Market Location used in regulated electricity markets.

A Market Location is a contract-level metering point identifier defined by the local jurisdiction (e.g., MaLo in Germany, MPAN in the UK, ESI-ID in the US, NMI in Australia). It abstracts from physical meters or channels and is the anchor for billing, settlement, reconciliation, forecasting, and portfolio aggregation.

Example Market Location Object

{
  "display_name": "Main Office – Consumption",
  "supported_directions": ["ENERGY_FLOW_DIRECTION_IMPORT"],
  "time_resolution": "TIME_RESOLUTION_15_MIN",
  "payload": {
    "cost_center": "CC-1103",
    "site_group": "HQ-North",
    "notes": "Primary billing meter"
  }
}

This describes the default metering interval (e.g., PT15M, PT30M, PT5M). It reflects the settlement granularity expected by the jurisdiction.

Note

Some markets provide multiple resolutions. This is metadata describing the primary resolution (e.g., PT15M).

Supported energy-flow directions for this Market Location.

Indicates which energy-flow directions this Market Location is permitted to represent according to regulatory or contractual rules.

What supported_directions means

This field reflects the contractual capability of the Market Location to represent import (consumption), export (generation), or both. It does not describe physical wiring or real-time flow, but the officially registered role in the market.

Market Location Examples

• Germany (DE) - Consumption MaLo → [IMPORT] - Feed-in MaLo → [EXPORT]

• UK (MPAN) - A single MPAN may support both directions → [IMPORT, EXPORT]

Meaning of Activation Status

This flag indicates whether the Market Location is operationally active:

docs.title: frequenz.api.marketmetering.v1alpha1.marketmetering_pb2.MarketLocationId
docs.text:
Bases: Message

Market-standard identifier describing a Market Location.

A Market Location is a jurisdiction-specific point of metering used for regulatory processes such as settlement, billing, supplier switching, balancing-group reconciliation, and DSO/TSO reporting. Different markets use incompatible identifier formats—varying in length, character sets, checksum rules, and decomposition.

This message encapsulates the official, market-issued identifier used to reference such a point. Examples: • Germany: MaLo-ID (Marktlokations-ID) • UK: MPAN (Meter Point Administration Number) • US: ESI-ID (Electric Service Identifier) • Australia NMI (National Metering Identifier)

Different markets use incompatible identifier formats—varying in length, character sets, checksum rules, and presentation formatting (spaces, hyphens, prefixes).

Example values for different markets

The following examples illustrate how the fields may be populated for different jurisdictions:

Market:Type Official ID Normalized Value DE:MALO_ID "12345678901" "12345678901" UK:MPAN "18 1066 1234 567 8901 234" "18106612345678901234" US_ERCOT:ESI_ID "10443720000012345" "10443720000012345" AU:NMI "NEM12-03456-A" "NEM1203456A"

In each case, value preserves the original format as provided by the market operator, while normalized_value is an implementation-specific cleaned representation suitable for validation, indexing, and comparisons.

docs.title: frequenz.api.marketmetering.v1alpha1.marketmetering_pb2.ReceiveMarketLocationSamplesStreamRequest
docs.text:
Bases: Message

Request for streaming time-series samples for one or more logical Market Locations.

Sample Series Expansion Logic

The server creates one independent time series for every unique combination of: • MarketLocationRef • EnergyFlowDirection • MetricType

Example: 2 Market Locations × 1 Direction × 2 Metrics = 4 series

Each of these is emitted as a separate MarketLocationSeries in the streamed response.

Example Request

The following example requests ENERGY samples for two Market Locations, both in IMPORT direction, over a 24-hour window:

{
  "market_location_refs": [
    {
      "enterprise_id": 42,
      "market_location_id": {
        "value": "DE01234567890",
        "type": "MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_MALO_ID"
      }
    },
    {
      "enterprise_id": 44,
      "market_location_id": {
        "value": "18 1066 1234 567 8901 234",
        "type": "MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_MPAN"
      }
    }
  ],
  "directions": [
    "ENERGY_FLOW_DIRECTION_IMPORT"
  ],
  "metric_types": [
    "METRIC_TYPE_ACTIVE_ENERGY"
  ],
  "stream_filter": {
    "revision_strategy": "REVISION_STRATEGY_LATEST_ONLY",
    "time_filter": {
      "interval": {
        "start_time": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",

      }
    },
    "resampling_options": {

    }
  }
}

docs.title: frequenz.api.marketmetering.v1alpha1.marketmetering_pb2.ReceiveMarketLocationSamplesStreamResponse
docs.text:
Bases: Message

Streaming response containing one or more time series fragments.

The service emits a distinct MarketLocationSeries message for every unique tuple of Market Location, EnergyFlowDirection and MetricType.

The RPC is a finite server-side stream: once all samples matching the request (across all Market Locations, directions, and metric types) have been delivered, the server closes the stream. However, if the request’s time_filter specifies no end_time, the stream continues in real time.

Consumers should treat each market location series in each streamed message as an independent, self-contained segment. Responses may be chunked.

Incremental / Chunked Streaming

The service may emit: • complete series in a single message, or • multiple incremental/chunked segments.

Sample Ordering & Updates

There is no guaranteed ordering between different series, between chunks of different series, or across series. A client MUST treat every received MarketLocationSeries as an independent, self-contained segment and merge or sort samples locally if ordering is required.

The service may also emit more than one sample with identical sample_time. This is normal and reflects the correction workflows required in regulated metering and real-time resampling.

A sample may be re-emitted whenever the service obtains better or newer information for that timestamp—whether through revised native readings, delayed arrivals, or updated resampling intervals.

Clients MUST deduplicate samples for the same sample_time by:

  1. Prefer the sample with the highest revision, when revisions are present, otherwise
  2. Prefer the sample with the latest update_time.

This rule applies uniformly to both native and resampled streams.

Example Response Fragment

Below is an example fragment of a streamed response for a request that queried IMPORT active energy values for a single Market Location over a 24-hour period (no downsampling or upsampling applied).

{
  "time_filter": {
    "interval": {
      "start_time": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "end_time":   "2025-01-02T00:00:00Z"
    }
  },
  "revision_strategy": "REVISION_STRATEGY_LATEST_ONLY",
  "resampling_options": {
    "resolution": "TIME_RESOLUTION_15_MIN",
    "downsampling_method": "DOWNSAMPLING_METHOD_MEAN"
  },
  "series": [
    {
      "market_location_ref": {
        "enterprise_id": 42,
        "market_location_id": {
          "value": "DE01234567890",
          "type": "MARKET_LOCATION_ID_TYPE_MALO_ID"
        }
      },
      "direction": "ENERGY_FLOW_DIRECTION_IMPORT",
      "metric_type": "METRIC_TYPE_ACTIVE_ENERGY",
      "metric_unit": "METRIC_UNIT_KWH",
      "resolution": "TIME_RESOLUTION_15_MIN",
      "samples": [
        {
          "sample_time": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
          "value": 1.234,
          "quality": "DATA_QUALITY_MEASURED",
          "revision": 1,
          "sample_update_time": "2025-01-01T00:00:02Z",
          "resampling_method": "RESAMPLING_METHOD_NATIVE"
        },
        {
          "sample_time": "2025-01-01T00:15:00Z",
          "value": 0.987,

docs.title: frequenz.api.marketmetering.v1alpha1.marketmetering_pb2.ResamplingOptions
docs.text:
Bases: Message

Resampling options for Market Location time-series data.

Resampling allows clients to request a time resolution that differs from the Market Location’s native stored resolution. The service constructs a uniform output grid based on the requested resolution and produces exactly one sample per interval.

Two semantic modes may result:

• Downsampling (when the requested resolution is coarser) Multiple native samples fall into one output interval; these are combined using the selected aggregation method.

• Upsampling (when the requested resolution is finer) Each native sample expands into multiple sub-intervals. ENERGY is allocated proportionally, while POWER is repeated stepwise.

In both cases the output sample timestamp equals the start of the interval in the materialized grid.

Example: Downsampling from 1-minute to 15-minute intervals

The stored time series has a native resolution of Δt = 1 minute. Resampling is requested with a resolution of ΔT = 15 minutes. In this case all native samples whose timestamps fall within an interval [t, t + Δt) contribute to the aggregated value for that interval. The timestamp of the aggregated sample is exactly t, the start of the interval.

For each interval k: Ik = [T0 + k·ΔT, T0 + (k+1)·ΔT)

The aggregated value A_k is the arithmetic mean of all samples whose timestamps ts satisfy: ts ∈ Ik

The resampled series consists of points: (t = T0 + k·ΔT, value = A_k)

Upsampling: 15-minute → 5-minute

If the native resolution is Δt = 15 min and the requested resolution is ΔT = 5 min, each native interval expands into three equally sized sub-intervals, with ENERGY proportionally allocated and POWER repeated.

docs.title: frequenz.api.marketmetering.v1alpha1.marketmetering_pb2.RevisionStrategy
docs.text:
Bases: _RevisionStrategy

Strategy for selecting which revisions of a resource should be returned.

Many entities in regulated energy systems evolve over time and may exist in multiple historical revisions. Examples include: • time-series samples that receive corrections or late updates • Market Location metadata updated by the user or backend processes

This enum allows clients to control whether they want only the most recent version of each entity or the full revision history.

Revision ordering

Revisions are ordered strictly by their numeric revision field. The service does not infer semantics from market-specific document types or timestamps — the highest numeric revision always represents the newest version of a given entity.

docs.text:

A SampleUpsertError describes why a sample could not be inserted or updated. It provides both a machine-readable classification and optional diagnostic information to support reconciliation and retry logic.

Error presence semantics

This message is present only when the upsert was rejected.

docs.text:
existing_sample() -> Global___MarketLocationSampleDetail

The stored sample that prevented this upsert.

Populated only when the service can identify an existing stored sample for the same tuple:

(market_location_ref, direction, metric_type, metric_unit, sample_time)

Behavior by error_code:

• REVISION_CONFLICT A sample with the same revision already exists but differs in payload. The returned sample has the same revision number.

• REVISION_TOO_OLD A newer revision already exists. The returned sample represents the latest stored revision (highest numeric revision).

• Other error codes This field is unset.

Important

existing_sample always refers to the same logical tuple as the request. It never refers to a different timestamp or metric.

docs.title: frequenz.api.marketmetering.v1alpha1.marketmetering_pb2.TimeFilter
docs.text:
Bases: Message

Filters records by a UTC time interval.

A metering sample represents a measured value for a fixed-resolution interval (e.g., 15 minutes). This filter restricts the returned samples to those whose interval start timestamps fall within an optional time window.

The time window is inclusive at the start and exclusive at the end

start_time ≤ sample_timestamp < end_time>

Filter Logic

  • interval is optional; if omitted, all timestamps are matched.
  • Only sample timestamps within the interval are included.
  • Interval semantics follow ISO 8601 conventions and match those used by other Frequenz services.

Example: All samples on or after a timestamp

{
  "interval": {
    "start_time": "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
}

Example: Samples in a closed-open time window

{
  "interval": {
    "start_time": "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z",
    "end_time":   "2025-06-02T00:00:00Z"
  }
}

docs.text:
interval() -> Interval

If omitted, samples from all timestamps are included.

docs.title: frequenz.api.marketmetering.v1alpha1.marketmetering_pb2.TimeResolution
docs.text:
Bases: _TimeResolution

Defines the time resolution (sampling interval) of metering data.

All timestamps refer to the start of the measured interval, and the interval runs until: [timestamp, timestamp + resolution)

Resolutions are modeled explicitly because different markets use different fixed intervals.

Common resolution examples

These intervals are commonly encountered in interval metering systems worldwide:

Jurisdiction Metric Type Resolution Germany (MaLo) Energy (kWh) PT15M UK (MPAN) Energy (kWh) PT30M Australia (NEM12) Energy (Wh) PT5M US (ERCOT) Power (kW) PT5M US (PJM/ISO-NE) Power/Energy PT1H Smart meters (AMI) Energy PT1M

Primary Resolution

A Market Location typically has one primary contractual resolution. Some systems may support additional resolutions (e.g., for telemetry or submetering).

docs.text:

Updates metadata of an existing Market Location.

Only a restricted subset of Market Location metadata may be updated. These rules preserve regulatory auditability and prevent retroactive changes that would conflict with historical billing, settlement, or reconciliation processes.

Updates always produce a new metadata revision. Historical revisions remain retrievable when using revision_strategy = REVISION_STRATEGY_ALL.

This field prevents lost updates when multiple callers update the same Market Location concurrently. Callers should first read the latest MarketLocationDetail, then pass its revision here. On mismatch, the service returns with an error indicating the current latest revision.

docs.title: frequenz.api.marketmetering.v1alpha1.marketmetering_pb2.UpsertMarketLocationSamplesStreamRequest
docs.text:
Bases: Message

A single ingestion event for one Market Location sample.

Each request message processes exactly one sample and produces one acknowledgement response.

The server performs strict validation of

• timestamp alignment with the Market Location's contractual resolution, • energy-flow direction against supported_directions, • metric_type against supported metrics, • metric_unit consistency with metric_type, • revision monotonicity for the (ML, direction, metric, timestamp) tuple.

Correction via revisioning (no deletion)

The MarketMeteringService never deletes samples. Regulated metering processes require a full historical audit trail.

A previously ingested sample is corrected by submitting a new revision with the same sample_time but a higher revision value.

Typical patterns: • Invalidate a value → send a new revision with quality = DATA_QUALITY_MISSING and value = 0. • Correct a value → send a new revision with the corrected value and quality = DATA_QUALITY_CORRECTED.

The backend selects the highest revision when serving data, while older revisions remain queryable via revision strategies.

Timestamp alignment is mandatory

sample.sample_time MUST align with the Market Location's contractual time_resolution.

Example: time_resolution = PT15M → allowed times are: 00:00, 00:15, 00:30, 00:45, ...

Misaligned timestamps are rejected. By default, the service rejects samples whose sample_time is in the future relative to the server clock and may also reject samples that are too far in the past.

Metric-unit consistency is validated

The provided metric_unit MUST be compatible with metric_type. ENERGY → {Wh, kWh, MWh} POWER → {W, kW, MW} REACTIVE_ENERGY → {VArh, kVArh, MVArh} REACTIVE_POWER → {VAr, kVAr, MVAr}

The backend does not perform unit conversion.

Direction and metric must be allowed

direction MUST be present in the Market Location's supported_directions. metric_type MUST be supported for ingestion by the service.

docs.text:

The physical unit of the value (e.g., kWh, kW).

MUST be coherent with metric_type; no implicit unit conversion occurs.

docs.title: frequenz.api.marketmetering.v1alpha1.marketmetering_pb2.UpsertMarketLocationSamplesStreamResponse
docs.text:
Bases: Message

Acknowledgement for a single sample upsert operation.

Each request message produces exactly one response message. The response ALWAYS echoes the attempted input sample, regardless of whether the operation succeeded or was rejected.

The presence of error determines whether the upsert was accepted:

• error unset → the sample was accepted (inserted or recognized as an idempotent no-op). • error set → the sample was rejected.

Echo semantics

The sample field always represents the client-submitted payload. It does NOT reflect server-side canonicalization or stored metadata. In particular, server-assigned timestamps (e.g. ingest_time) are returned separately.
